facts.text: McConnellsburg was laid out by Daniel McConnell on April 20, 1786, and officially incorporated on March 26, 1814.
The borough sits in a 2‑mile‑wide valley between Tuscarora Mountain and Meadow Grounds Mountain in the Appalachian Ridge and Valley region.
McConnellsburg’s historic district, listed on the National Register in 1993, contains 144 buildings that include the original Fulton House and the log cabin of its founder.
Today, Oshkosh Corporation’s JLG Industries, a major maker of boomlifts and other lifting equipment, is the borough’s largest employer.
The town is a key stop on Pennsylvania’s largest barn‑quilt trail, hosting more than 200 colorful quilts that attract art lovers from across the state.
The Fulton County Courthouse, built in 1850, still serves as the county’s judicial center and is a prominent landmark in downtown McConnellsburg.
